Kleren Anisette

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Makes about 1 quart (1 liter)Prep 10 min

Kleren Anisette is a traditional Haitian anise-flavored spirit often enjoyed during the Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa. This festival celebrates the agricultural spirit and the harvest season, and Kleren Anisette is cherished for its sweet, aromatic qualities that complement the festive meals and rituals.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (480 ml) white cane alcohol or neutral grain spirit
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) anise seeds
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water

Method

  1. In a clean glass jar, combine the anise seeds and white cane alcohol.
  2. Seal the jar tightly and let it infuse in a cool, dark place for 3 days, shaking gently once a day.
  3. In a small saucepan, combine the sugar and water and heat gently until the sugar dissolves completely to make a simple syrup. Let it cool.
  4. Strain the anise-infused alcohol through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a clean container to remove the seeds.
  5. Slowly add the cooled simple syrup to the strained anise alcohol and stir well to combine.
  6. Bottle the Kleren Anisette and let it rest for at least 2 days before serving to allow flavors to meld.
  7. Serve chilled or at room temperature, traditionally in small glasses during the Fete de Papa Zaka celebrations.

Tips

  • Use high-quality white cane alcohol or a neutral grain spirit for the best flavor.
  • Adjust the sugar syrup amount to taste for a sweeter or drier anisette.
  • For a stronger anise flavor, increase the infusion time up to 5 days but be cautious of bitterness.
